items.expected_claim: benchmark evaluating model-guided discovery: train on historical MP data (~154k structures), predict stability of ~215k new structures from WBM dataset
metric is F1 on correctly identifying thermodynamically stable structures; tests full pipeline including structure relaxation quality
leaderboard tracks universal MLIPs (MACE, CHGNet, M3GNet, SevenNet, EquiformerV2) and GNN property models across discovery-relevant tasks

13-task benchmark for inorganic solid-state property prediction spanning 312 to 132,752 samples; properties include formation energy, band gap, bulk/shear moduli, refractive index, and phonon frequency from DFT and experimental sources

crystal graph neural networks (CGCNN, MEGNet) outperform descriptor-based and AutoML methods on tasks with ≥10,000 samples; smaller datasets favour Automatminer, a fully automated feature-extraction and model-selection pipeline
uses consistent 5-fold nested cross-validation with MAE (regression) and ROC-AUC (classification) metrics; reference algorithm is Automatminer
NIST database of ~56,000 materials with DFT-computed band structures, elastic constants, piezoelectric tensors, dielectric response, and topological properties
one of three major open DFT databases alongside Materials Project and OQMD, enabling cross-database validation of property prediction models
provides training and evaluation data for deep learning models across formation energy, bandgap, DOS, IR spectra, and 2D exfoliation energy prediction tasks
>150,000 inorganic compounds with DFT-computed energy, band gap, elastic, magnetic, dielectric properties via GGA/GGA+U
provides REST API with >10M monthly calls; primary source for training universal MLIPs (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE-MP)
reference database for thermodynamic convex hull stability — underpins most MLIP benchmarks for stability prediction
Materials Project Trajectory dataset of 1,580,395 DFT single-point calculations from GGA/GGA+U ionic relaxation trajectories, providing energies, forces, stresses, and magnetic moments
backbone dataset used to train CHGNet and MACE-MP universal potentials; covers 89 elements excluding noble gases and actinoids
provides comprehensive coverage of diverse chemical space with over 145,000 distinct compounds represented across the trajectory frames
Open Quantum Materials Database: >1,000,000 DFT structures from ICSD experimental entries and crystal structure prototypes
uses PBE functional; particularly strong coverage of binary and ternary compounds for phase diagram and stability benchmarking
frequently used alongside Materials Project for benchmarking stability prediction and formation energy models

Automatic Flow database with >625,000 compounds (2015; >3.5M by 2022) covering binary alloys, Heusler intermetallics, and ICSD experimental structures with standardized high-throughput DFT settings (PBE+PAW)
defines reproducible DFT parameter sets — k-point density, smearing, convergence thresholds, DFT+U for d/f-block elements — ensuring cross-material comparability
uses standardized Brillouin zone k-point paths for band structure calculations, enabling systematic electronic structure comparison across materials
dataset of ~175,000 stable and metastable inorganic crystals (within 100 meV/atom of the convex hull) computed with PBEsol and SCAN functionals using VASP (PAW, forces converged to 5 meV/Å)
tabulated properties include total energies, volumes, band gaps, total magnetic moments, and stress tensor components from both PBEsol and SCAN, enabling functional-comparison benchmarking
designed for training ML models for solid-state property prediction; freely available on the Materials Cloud repository as pymatgen-compatible ComputedStructureEntry JSON files

2.2 million DFT-relaxed crystal structures predicted stable relative to the Materials Project / OQMD / ICSD convex hull; 381,000 lie on the updated hull as newly discovered stable materials — ~10× expansion over all previously known stable crystals
all calculations use VASP with PAW-PBE functional at 520 eV cutoff, Materials Project workflow DFT+U corrections for select transition metals, and a two-stage relaxation + static calculation protocol

GNoME ionic-relaxation trajectory data was used to pretrain a NequIP equivariant interatomic potential that achieves zero-shot ionic conductivity prediction on 623 unseen compositions, outperforming M3GNet and CHGNet potentials trained on smaller datasets

189,981 candidate crystal structures generated by iterative chemical-element substitution from 9,524 Materials Project seed compounds, spanning a broad composition space beyond the training distribution

18,479 structures confirmed on the DFT convex hull (PBE/VASP), achieving a 9.72% discovery success rate; serves as the standard out-of-distribution test set in the Matbench Discovery benchmark (~215k unique-prototype subset used by Riebesell 2025)
stable compounds are annotated with band gaps, magnetic moments, and hardness; dataset publicly deposited and used to evaluate the generalization of universal MLIPs to unseen chemical space

~118 million inorganic bulk crystal DFT single-points, relaxations, and AIMD trajectories labeled with energies, forces, and stresses; generated by FAIR (Meta) at a cost of >400 million CPU core hours

calculations use VASP with GGA-PBE (PBE+U for oxides/fluorides with Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Mo, Ni, V, W) following Materials Project conventions but with VASP pseudopotential v5.4, introducing ~52 meV/atom mean energy offset vs. MP
EquiformerV2 models (31M–154M parameters) pre-trained on OMat24 and fine-tuned on MPtrj + sAlexandria achieve F1 = 0.916 on Matbench Discovery — the first model to exceed F1 = 0.9 on that leaderboard
